crux: depth ratio k = Z_near/Z_far of the front tyres' outer faces: 0.915 (round 1) vs 0.923 (C1/C2), i.e. the far tyre's outer-face centre at row ~863 vs ~866
fault_found: C1/C2 read the far tyre's silhouette 28-43 px below its centre, where the nearer inner face takes over the silhouette; own fits give far centre row 862.8-864.0 (k 0.9145-0.918) and an axle-parallax slope of 0.912-0.914, not 0.923
lesson: When a depth ratio comes from a silhouette of a cylinder seen obliquely, use only the arc that belongs to the intended end face (compute where the other face's circle takes over from the face offset), and prefer a free-intercept regression over per-frame ratios, which absorb any assumed-radius or edge-bias offset.
